description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of various models on a classification task, with the y-axis representing accuracy ranging from 40% to 65% in 5% increments and the x-axis displaying five different model configurations. The models compared are RoBERTa w/o Exp. (light gray), LaSQuE (mean) (orange), LaSQuE (green), LaSQuE (syn2real) (purple), and LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) (dark gray). The RoBERTa w/o Exp. model achieves an accuracy of approximately 46%. The LaSQuE (mean) model shows an accuracy of about 47%, while the LaSQuE (syn2real) model reaches approximately 59%. The LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) model demonstrates the highest performance, with an accuracy of around 62%. The LaSQuE (mean) and LaSQuE (syn2real) models show similar performance, with the LaSQuE (syn2real) model slightly outperforming the LaSQuE (mean) model. The LaSQuE (syn2real + curriculum) model significantly outperforms all other models, indicating the effectiveness of curriculum learning in improving zero-shot classification accuracy.
